id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

typeIdent.description:
Indicates explicit sub-type of entry.  Composed of the concatenation of the typeKey of the instance's type and all
of its base type's typeIdent

facility.description: The Facility associated with the WorkOrder

status.description:
The status of the WorkOrder. Enumerated via {@link WorkOrderStatusEnum}.
Defaults to {@link WorkOrderStatusEnum#CREATED}.

statusCode.description:
The status code for the WorkOrder
Customer-specific codes indicating current status of the work order, e.g. Assigned to field

workOrderNumber.description:
The WorkOrder number specified
A customer-specific identifier for the work order. Not used internally as a key

workOrderType.description:
The type of the WorkOrder
The highest-level classification for a work order, e.g. customer requested in region X.

workSubtype.description:
The work subtype of the WorkOrder
A finer distinction within a workType
e.g. work type might indicate a reconnect of power
work sub type might indicate because the customer has paid their back bill
or indicate that a new customer has moved in

workType.description:
The work type of the WorkOrder, is a property on the parentWorkOrder
The type of work order, describes the actual work that must be done for the work order
e.g. reconnection of power

workStartDate.description: The work start date of the WorkOrder

workEndDate.description:
The work end date of the WorkOrder
The more important of the two dates in most metrics as it indicates when to start looking for aberrant behavior

openedDate.description: The opened date for the WorkOrder

comments.description: Allows back office or field investigators to provide other important information about the work order

resolution.description:
The resolution of the WorkOrder
e.g. "Completed Job" or "Confirmed - Unable to bill"

resolutionTime.description:
The time it took to resolve the WorkOrder
specified by ExactDimension with value and unit of measurement

timestamp.description:
The timestamp on the WorkOrder
Usually used to indicate when the work order was created
while workStartDate and workEndDate indicate the actual work time span

serviceGroup.description: The service group responsible for the WorkOrder

serviceTeam.description: The service team within the service group responsible for the WorkOrder

technician.description: The technician associated with the WorkOrder

asset.description: The asset associated with the WorkOrder

customer.description: The customer associated with the WorkOrder

location.description: The location associated with the WorkOrder

customerOrg.description: The organization associated with the WorkOrder

parentWorkOrder.description: The original WorkOrder created, this could have subtasks such as child WorkOrders or WorkItems

childWorkOrders.description:
Separate work orders spawned from the original WorkOrder.
In Enel, for a while we stored WorkItems in WorkOrder and used childWorkOrders to link them,
but that was confusing and made the WorkOrder table too large to be performant.

workItems.description:
The work items for the WorkOrder
specific sub-tasks that are associated with the work order.

reasonCode.description: The internal code that corresponds with the reason for the work order

symptomCode.description: Symptom code of the work order to help understand root cause.

causeText.description: Cause text of the work order to help understand root cause.

parent.description: {@link ReliabilityAsset} associated with the work order.

maintActivityType.description: Type of the maintenance activity of this work order.

displayStatus.description: A translated representation of {@link WorkOrder#status} to be used in the UI.

workDueDate.description: The date that the work order is due.

maintItem.description: Reference to {@link Item} for maintenance in this work order.

uiPartStatus.description: A translated representation of {@link WorkOrder#partStatus} to be used in the UI.

workOrderPriority.description:
The priority field that is populated directly from customer data source.
We don't know what values would be in here so we don't use enum field of priority. DS team will decide how to map this field to priority.

workOrderPartsSimilarity.description: The list of similar parts from work orders tied to this work order from {@link WorkOrderPartsSimilarityPredictions}.

requiredStartDatetime.description: Date time when work order was requested.

codingIncludingTextField.description: Coding that includes text field to help understand the root cause.

apparentCause.description: Apparent cause of the work order to help understand root cause.

partStatus.description: The status of the parts for the WorkOrder. Enumerated via {@link WorkOrderPartStatusEnum}

preventiveMaintenanceType.description: This is the preventive maintenance type for this work order, if applicable.

partsListInventory.description:
The list of parts associated with this work order tied to {@link InventorySeries}.
The structure is a map, with the {@link InventorySeries} id as the key and the quantity avaliable
at the time the work order is to be executed as the value.

workOrderCost.description: The maintenance cost of the work order (worker cost + plant loss + parts cost)

priority.description: The priority of the work order.

creationDate.description: The creation date for the workorder, to be used in UI.

partsList.description:
The list of parts associated with this work order tied to {@link InventorySeries}.
The structure is a map, with the {@link InventorySeries} id as the key and the quantity as the value.

workOrderSimilarity.description: The list of similar work orders tied to this work order from {@link WorkOrderSimilarityPredictions}.

failureMode.description:
The failure mode for this work order, if applicable.
This should come from the `name` field in {@link FailureMode}.

createdBy.description:
{@link User} who created this work order.
Calculated by piping `meta.createdBy` through {@link ReliabilityExpressionEngineFunction#userInformation}.

functionalLocation.description: Functional location that ensures connection between work order and subsystem.

priorityDescription.description: Description according to the priority code.

assignee.description: {@link User} who has been assigned to perform this work order.

totalActCosts.description: Total cost of activity to identify importance of the work order.

assetCase.description: {@link ReliabilityAssetCase} associated with the work order.

assigneeName.description:
Display name for the {@link assignee}.
Calculated from assignee's `firstName` or `lastName`. If either exists, it trims and concatenates them to display the full name.
If neither `firstName` nor `lastName` exists, it checks if assignee.email exists, and if so, returns the email.
If email doesn't exist either, it falls back to returning `name` field of assignee.
